title: The Jamāʿa of 1379 takes up the question of the capital. The expansion north has left Gharnāṭa isolated, a long ride from the frontier, and the court finds itself cut off from its slowly integrating lands. The old idea of a capital at Qurṭuba is raised again, and then a second proposal: invest in the sea, set the Catalan shipwrights, now the Emperor's subjects, to building a trading fleet, and move the capital to Ishbīliya, where its power would reach furthest. The assembly and the Emperor choose Ishbīliya

proposals.Qurṭuba: the old idea: the caliphs' capital, at the centre of al-Andalus
proposals.Ishbīliya: a capital on the river and the sea, with a trading fleet built by the Catalan shipwrights

data.why: Gharnāṭa is far from the northern frontier and from the new lands; the court is decentralised from them
data.outcome: the assembly and the Emperor decide to move the capital to Ishbīliya; the move is due to be complete by the end of November 1379 (Trent's account)
data.date: late April 1379 (Trent); the exact day awaits a save

title: Ishbīliya will be the capital by the end of November. To tie it into the realm the Emperor orders new roads at great cost, to Sharīsh and Mālaqa and north to Baṭalyaws and Ṭulayṭula, and borrows from the estates to pay for them
